newsitem.title: UK: Lower non-OPEC supply gives extra room to OPEC-IEA.
newsitem.headline: Lower non-OPEC supply gives extra room to OPEC-IEA.

text.p: Oil supplies from non-OPEC producers will not hit the heights previously expected at the end of this year and demand will be higher, leaving extra room for OPEC crude on world markets, the International Energy Agency said on Tuesday.

Global demand in the fourth quarter is now projected at 73.7 million barrels a day (bpd), a 100,000 bpd upward revision on last month's estimate, the Paris-based energy watchdog said in its monthly oil market report.
Year-on-year, the world's thirst for oil is expected to grow a sharp 1.7 million bpd in 1996 and a further 1.8 million bpd in 1997.
The agency revised down its previous estimate for fourth quarter supplies from producers outside the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Counties (OPEC) by 200,000 bpd to 45.0 million bpd.
But that is still is a whopping 1.5 million rise over the third quarter and an even more impressive 2.3 million over fourth quarter 1995.
Demand for OPEC oil and stocks in the fourth quarter has been boosted by 300,000 bpd to 25.9 million bpd, close to current production of about 25.88 million bpd.
Non-OPEC oil supplies rose strongly in September, carrying world production up 900,000 bpd on the month to 72.53 million, the IEA said.
"The non-OPEC supply growth was concentrated in the UK, Norway and the US, but significant gains also occurred in China, Brazil, Canada and Mexico," it said.

But its demand estimate for the first quarter 1997 was revised down 100,000 bpd to 74.7 million "with a downward revision to former Soviet Union demand more than offsetting an upward adjustment to Chinese demand."
It also shaved 100,000 bpd apiece from non-OPEC supply estimates for each of the first three quarters of next year.
Non-OPEC supply on average for next year is revised down by by 100,000 bpd to 45.5 million bpd, a rise of 1.8 million over 1996.
